# YouTube (as a podcast destination)

- Category: destination
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md).

| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| multi_show         | YouTube Studio has a dedicated "Podcasts" content type per channel, and RSS ingestion/connection is configured per podcast under Content > Podcasts > Details. There is no documented "network" object spanning multiple channels/shows under one account beyond Google's separate Content Manager/MCN tooling for large partners; ordinary creator accounts manage each show as its own channel.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26), [Publish or disconnect episodes from an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13973017) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| roles_approvals    | YouTube Studio "channel permissions" define account-level roles: Owner, Manager, Editor, Editor (limited), Viewer, and Viewer (limited), assignable per channel without sharing the Google account password. Content Manager (for verified partners) additionally supports fully custom roles with checkbox-level permissions. Neither is scoped per-show within one channel, and there is no documented review/approval-before-publish gate beyond the fact that RSS-ingested episodes upload as private videos for manual review before the owner/manager/editor publishes them.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | [Add or remove access to your YouTube channel with channel permissions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9481328) (2026-09-26), [Create and manage roles (Content Manager)](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/4525580) (2026-09-26), [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26)                                                                      |
| video              | Native video hosting/publishing is core to YouTube; podcast video can be uploaded directly or generated automatically from an RSS audio feed (static-image video from show art). Apple Podcasts HLS video partner status: **does not apply** — YouTube is a destination/platform in its own right, not a hosting backend submitting content to Apple's HLS video partner program; trade-press lists of Apple HLS video partners (iOS 26.4) name hosting companies such as Acast, ART19, Triton's Omny Studio, SiriusXM Media/AdsWizz/Simplecast, Transistor, Audiomeans, PodBean, Captivate, RSS.com, Podigee, Podspace, Riverside, Ausha, and Firstory — YouTube is not on it and the concept doesn't apply to YouTube's own destination product.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | [Apple introduces a new video podcast experience](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/02/apple-introduces-a-new-video-podcast-experience-on-apple-podcasts/) (2026-09-26, third-party/Apple), [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                              |
| transcripts        | YouTube auto-generates captions/transcripts for uploaded video podcasts (its own captions system, editable in Studio); it is a video-caption feature, not a podcast RSS transcript. There is no documented support for reading/importing the `podcast:transcript` RSS tag when ingesting a feed — ingestion docs describe only audio-to-video conversion and episode metadata, not transcript files. Undocumented whether YouTube writes out a `podcast:transcript`-style artifact anywhere; treat as undocumented.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26) — no mention of `podcast:transcript`; captions/auto-caption behavior is general YouTube product knowledge, not confirmed against a fetched help page in this session, so treat that detail as third-party-sourced pending direct citation                                                                                  |
| comments_community | Standard YouTube video comments apply to podcast episode/video pages. Creators also get the channel Community tab (posts, polls, images) and, once monetized, Channel Memberships with members-only posts, badges, and custom emoji as community/audience perks. These are channel-wide features, not podcast-feed-specific.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | [Get started with channel memberships on YouTube](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7636690) (2026-09-26), [Create or manage your channel's membership levels & perks](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7544492) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| analytics          | YouTube Studio Analytics plus the YouTube Analytics API (channel/video-level metrics, OAuth scope `yt-analytics.readonly` / `yt-analytics-monetary.readonly`) and the YouTube Reporting API (scheduled bulk CSV-style report jobs) cover audience, watch time, and revenue data. IAB Tech Lab Podcast Measurement certification status: undocumented — no YouTube help or developer page found claiming IAB Podcast Measurement Technical Guidelines certification, and IAB Tech Lab's own compliant-companies list (spot-checked via search) surfaced only third-party measurement vendors (e.g., Magellan AI), not YouTube itself; treat YouTube as **not certified / undocumented**, not "not supported," since no explicit disclaimer from either party was found.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | [YouTube Analytics and Reporting APIs — Introduction](https://developers.google.com/youtube/reporting) (2026-09-26), [YouTube Reporting API reports](https://developers.google.com/youtube/reporting/v1/reports) (2026-09-26); [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/) (2026-09-26), not listed in the registry                                                      |
| private_premium    | YouTube supports "unlisted" and "private" video visibility, and (once a channel is monetized via YPP) "member-only" videos, live streams, Shorts, and posts restricted to paying Channel Members across creator-set tiers ($0.99–$99.99/month, up to several tiers). This is YouTube's own paywall (channel memberships), not a portable private RSS feed — there is no documented mechanism to ingest or expose an external private/premium podcast RSS feed (e.g., password-protected feed URL) as a private feed on YouTube.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | [Get started with channel memberships on YouTube](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7636690) (2026-09-26), [Use & manage your channel membership benefits](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14917424) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| dai_programmatic   | YouTube sells its own in-stream ads (pre-roll, mid-roll, display) via the YouTube Partner Program/Google ad systems, with automatic and manual mid-roll placement controls in Studio; this is YouTube's proprietary ad system, not a dynamic-ad-insertion (DAI) product that lets a podcast host stitch third-party programmatic ads into the audio/video file itself. No documented open programmatic marketplace or DAI feature for podcast RSS-ingested content; region/eligibility for monetization is gated entirely by YPP eligibility (country availability, subscriber/watch-time thresholds). Undocumented whether ingested podcast episodes (vs. natively uploaded video) are eligible for the same ad formats — the RSS ingestion page states podcast content itself "cannot include advertisements" inserted by the creator without disclosure, which is a content policy, not a DAI feature.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | [Manage mid-roll ad breaks in long videos](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6175006) (2026-09-26), [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26), [YouTube Partner Program overview & eligibility](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                |
| api_export         | **Data API v3** (read/write): OAuth2, supports `videos.insert` (upload, quota cost 1 unit within a separate "Video Uploads" quota bucket, default cap 100 calls/day, 256GB max file size, scopes `youtube.upload`/`youtube`/`youtubepartner`/`youtube.force-ssl`), plus read/write for playlists, channels, captions, etc. **Compliance audits**: any Data API project created after July 28, 2020 has uploaded videos forced to private-only until the project completes a compliance audit with Google; the same audit is required to raise quota above the small default allocation (100 `search.list`, 100 `videos.insert`, 10,000 units/day combined for everything else). **Analytics/Reporting**: YouTube Analytics API (query-style, near-real-time metrics) and YouTube Reporting API (scheduled bulk report jobs, CSV-like downloadable reports) both via OAuth2 with `yt-analytics.readonly`/`yt-analytics-monetary.readonly` scopes. **Bulk export**: no documented one-click "export all my podcast RSS/media" tool from Studio itself; **Google Takeout** covers a personal Google/YouTube data export (uploaded video files, watch/comment/playlist history, channel data) as zip/tgz archives, which is the closest documented bulk-export path. Webhooks: undocumented for podcast/video publish events (YouTube offers PubSubHubbub feed notifications for channel uploads, but that's a legacy, video-only mechanism, not documented in current podcast context — treat as undocumented here). | [videos.insert](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos/insert) (2026-09-26), [Quota and Compliance Audits](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/guides/quota_and_compliance_audits) (2026-09-26), [YouTube Analytics and Reporting APIs](https://developers.google.com/youtube/reporting) (2026-09-26), [Download your Google data (Takeout)](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/3024190) (2026-09-26) |
| custom_domains     | YouTube does not support custom/vanity domains for channel or feed hosting. It offers auto-generated "handle" URLs (`youtube.com/@handle`) as the current channel-URL customization mechanism; legacy "custom URLs" (`youtube.com/c/...`) still work for channels that already had one but can no longer be newly created. There is no concept of a podcast RSS feed URL on YouTube (ingestion is a one-way pull, not a rehosted feed) and therefore no documented 301 feed-redirect or feed-portability mechanism — "leaving" YouTube just means disconnecting the RSS feed (per the publish/disconnect help page) and deleting/unpublishing the generated videos; the original audio host and its feed are unaffected since YouTube only ever pulled from it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | [Custom URL overview](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2657968) (2026-09-26), [Understand your YouTube channel's URLs](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/6180214) (2026-09-26), [Publish or disconnect episodes from an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13973017) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                              |
| pricing_2_show     | YouTube itself is **free** to publish on — there is no plan/tier fee for uploading video or connecting an RSS feed to a channel; monetization (ads, memberships, Supers) is opt-in and revenue-share based, not a subscription cost. For the "small pilot" scenario (2 shows, weekly audio+video, ~10k downloads/mo, 3 staff seats, one private/premium feed): $0/month to host and publish 2 shows as 2 channels with unlimited seats via channel permissions (Owner/Manager/Editor/Viewer, no per-seat fee documented); the "private/premium feed" requirement would map to Channel Memberships, which requires YPP monetization eligibility (1,000 subscribers + 4,000 public watch hours in 12 months, or 500 subscribers/3,000 watch hours for the newer early-access tier) — a brand-new pilot show would likely not yet qualify, so premium/member-only content is "contact sales / unpublished" in the sense that it cannot be turned on until audience thresholds are met; there's no dollar price for it once eligible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | [YouTube Partner Program overview & eligibility](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851) (2026-09-26), [Get started with channel memberships](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7636690) (2026-09-26), [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26)                                                                                                    |

## Integration surface

- **API:** YouTube Data API v3 (REST, OAuth 2.0) — read/write for videos, playlists, channels, captions; `videos.insert` for uploads (1 unit of a separate Video Uploads bucket, default 100 calls/day). Default overall quota is 10,000 units/day for all other endpoints combined, plus separate small default buckets (100 `search.list`, 100 `videos.insert`); raising any of these requires a Google compliance audit. Uploads from any API project created after 2020-07-28 are forced to private until that project passes audit. [videos.insert](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/docs/videos/insert) (2026-09-26), [Quota and Compliance Audits](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/guides/quota_and_compliance_audits) (2026-09-26)
- **Analytics/Reporting:** YouTube Analytics API (query/near-real-time) and YouTube Reporting API (scheduled bulk report jobs), both OAuth 2.0 with `yt-analytics.readonly` / `yt-analytics-monetary.readonly` scopes. [YouTube Analytics and Reporting APIs](https://developers.google.com/youtube/reporting) (2026-09-26)
- **Webhooks:** No current, documented podcast/video-publish webhook product was found in this session; undocumented for this use case (legacy PubSubHubbub channel-upload notifications exist in general YouTube product history but weren't confirmed against a fetched current doc, so treated as undocumented here).
- **Export formats:** Data API read endpoints (JSON) for metadata; Google Takeout for a personal bulk export (uploaded video files, comments, playlists, watch history) as zip/tgz. No documented one-step "export my whole channel as RSS" tool — YouTube is a one-way RSS _consumer_, not a re-publisher of a portable feed. [Download your Google data](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/3024190) (2026-09-26)
- **SSO / auth:** All API access is Google OAuth 2.0 (Google account/Google Cloud project); no SAML/enterprise SSO documented for the Data/Analytics/Reporting APIs. Studio access uses regular Google account sign-in plus channel permissions roles. [Add or remove access to your YouTube channel with channel permissions](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9481328) (2026-09-26)
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) RSS ingestion is one-directional and lossy — YouTube generates its own video assets from show art and does not resync edits or re-uploaded audio automatically, so corrections must be redone manually on YouTube; (2) no custom domain/feed portability — there is no YouTube-hosted RSS feed to "move" elsewhere, so any audience built natively on YouTube (subscribers, comments, memberships, watch history, algorithmic recommendations) is non-portable; (3) API upload quota is small by default (100 `videos.insert`/day) and any production integration needs a Google compliance audit to scale or to escape the forced-private-on-upload restriction, which is a real dependency/approval risk for Relay if it ever automates publishing to YouTube; (4) monetization features (memberships, Supers) are gated behind YPP subscriber/watch-time thresholds, not available on demand like Relay's own private-feed model. [Deliver podcasts using an RSS feed](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13525207) (2026-09-26), [Quota and Compliance Audits](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/guides/quota_and_compliance_audits) (2026-09-26), [YouTube Partner Program overview & eligibility](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851) (2026-09-26)

## Narrative (≤150 words)

YouTube is a free, high-reach _destination_ for podcast video/audio, not a host Relay would build against as infrastructure. RSS ingestion auto-converts audio episodes to static-image videos and stages them private for review — a crude approval step, not Relay's editorial workflow with an immutable release record. Multi-show and roles exist only as ordinary multi-channel + channel-permissions administration, with no per-show scoping or premium-feed concept; "private" content means YPP-gated Channel Memberships, unrelated to portable private RSS. Transcripts are YouTube's own video captions, not `podcast:transcript`-aware. Analytics are strong (Data/Analytics/Reporting APIs) but IAB Podcast Measurement certification is undocumented. Apple's HLS video partner program doesn't apply to YouTube at all. The real dependency risk for Relay is API upload quota (100/day default, forced-private uploads pending a Google compliance audit) and total non-portability — there is no YouTube feed to export or redirect away from.

- Could not find a YouTube or IAB page directly confirming or denying IAB Tech Lab Podcast Measurement certification for YouTube; marked "undocumented" per the brief's rule rather than "not supported."
- Captions/auto-transcript behavior for uploaded video and the `podcast:transcript` RSS-tag non-support are based on general knowledge plus search snippets, not a single authoritative fetched YouTube help page confirming auto-caption generation — flagged inline in the transcripts row.
- No page required login or failed to load in this session; all cited pages were reachable via WebFetch/WebSearch summaries.
- Apple HLS video partner list is third-party sourced (Apple newsroom + press coverage) since the brief's own suggested Apple page wasn't directly fetched by name; used Apple's own newsroom post as the primary citation, which is not third-party.
